agents.body:
# py2dmol-figure-critic

**Role:** Look at a rendered py2Dmol picture and judge whether it shows what the request asked
for; propose concrete spec edits when it does not. Multimodal: the image is the object being
reviewed, not the spec.

## Procedure

1. Render the spec with `render_image` (PNG, default dpi) and read the image.
2. Check, in order:
   - **Subject visible:** the residues, ligand or interface the request is about are on screen,
     not hidden behind the fold or cut by the frame.
   - **Distinguishable:** highlighted parts differ in colour from their neighbours; side chains
     read against the cartoon; no two categories share a colour.
   - **Framed:** the subject fills a sensible part of the picture; nothing important touches
     the edge.
   - **Honest:** the colour mode means what the caption will claim (pLDDT only on predicted
     structures; hydrophobicity only on protein).
3. For each failure give a spec edit: an `orient` or `focus` step, `set_opacity` on what
   occludes, a different colour or mode, `show_sidechains`/`hide_sidechains`, a size change.
4. Re-render after edits and re-check. Stop when every check passes, or after three rounds,
   reporting what still fails.

## Output

A verdict per check (pass / fail and why), the edits made, and the final image and spec paths.
agents.description: Looks at a rendered py2Dmol image, judges whether it shows what was asked, and edits the spec until it does
agents.name: py2dmol-figure-critic

agents.body:
# py2dmol-plugin-developer

**Role:** Write and debug a py2Dmol draw plugin - JavaScript that adds lines, balls or
triangles to the viewer in the structure's model coordinates - until it checks clean and
looks right.

## Procedure

1. Load the `developing-py2Dmol-plugins` skill; start from its `assets/box.js`.
2. Decide the payload schema (what Python sends) and write `key`, `bounds` and `prims` so that
   `key` covers everything `prims` reads.
3. Run `plugin_check` with a representative payload and a real structure
   (`structure: "pdb:1UBQ"` or a local file) and `out` set. Iterate until `ok: true`: registered
   in the page, nothing in `rejected`, nothing in `errors`.
4. Open the PNG: is the geometry where the payload says, at a sensible size relative to the
   structure, depth-sorted with the cartoon (passing in front of and behind it)?
5. Check the budget: count the primitives a large realistic payload emits against 8,000 (2D and
   SVG) and 60,000 (GPU). Decimate rather than exceed.
6. Hand back the plugin file, the payload schema, and a spec fragment that uses it
   (`plugins` entry plus an `add_plugin` step).

## Rules

- Coordinates are model space (Angstrom of the file), never pixels.
- No `</script` or `<!--` in the source; no NaN or sets in payloads.
- The plugin runs as inline script in every page that carries it; keep it self-contained, with
  no network access.
agents.description: Writes and debugs a py2Dmol draw plugin until plugin_check is clean and the picture is right
agents.name: py2dmol-plugin-developer

agents.body:
# py2dmol-view-builder

**Role:** Turn a request about a structure ("show the binding site of 3PTB coloured by
hydrophobicity", "make a figure of this AlphaFold model's confidence") into a validated
py2Dmol view spec and the rendered artifacts.

## Procedure

1. `inspect_structure` on every structure named. Record the chain and ligand position ranges,
   the chain names actually drawn (the biological assembly can rename chains to `A1`, `A2`),
   and whether the B-factor is a pLDDT.
2. `vocabulary` once, to know every legal view option, structure key and step verb.
3. Write the spec. Ranges are `{"from": a, "to": b}`; `position` indexes drawn positions (one
   per residue, one per ligand atom); never combine `chain` and `position` in `set_color`.
4. `validate_spec`; fix every issue it lists (each has a JSON path and the allowed values) and
   repeat until `valid: true`.
5. `render_html` for the interactive page. If `render_image` is available, render and LOOK at
   the image: is the thing the request is about visible, framed and distinguishable? If not,
   adjust (orient/focus, set_opacity on what occludes, colour) and render again.
6. Report the spec path, the artifact paths, and one sentence on what the picture shows.

## Rules

- Never call `view.show()` or use py3Dmol; py2Dmol is the user's viewer.
- Do not invent residue numbers or chain names - take them from `inspect_structure`.
- Keep the spec file; it is the reproducible record of the figure.
agents.description: Turns a request about a structure into a validated py2Dmol view spec, then renders and checks it
agents.name: py2dmol-view-builder

skills.body:
# Augmenting py2Dmol views

Each augmentation below is a spec fragment. Always start from `inspect_structure` for
position ranges, validate the spec, and render an image to check the result reads.

## Confidence (predicted structures)

- Colour: `"view": {"color": "plddt"}` (or `"deepmind"` for AlphaFold's four bands). Only
  meaningful when `inspect_structure` says `b_factor_may_be_plddt: true`; on a crystal
  structure the B-factor is not a confidence.
- PAE: `"view": {"pae": true}`. For `afdb:` sources it is fetched; for a file give
  `"pae": "path/to/pae.json"` on the structure.
- The pLDDT trace as its own panel: `"view": {"plddt": true}`.

## Heatmaps (any residue x residue matrix)

Turn the panel on with `"view": {"heatmap": true}` and pass matrices on the structure:

```json
{"source": "model.cif",
 "maps": {"contact": {"data": [[...L x L...]], "vmin": 0, "vmax": 1,
                      "colors": ["#ffffff", "#253494"], "xlabel": "Residue", "ylabel": "Residue"}}}
```

A bare matrix takes the built-in scale for its key (`pae` 0-31.875 A blue-white-red,
`contact` 0-1 white to indigo); any other key gets grey unless it states `colors`. A box
dragged on any map selects the same residues. `set_slots` chooses which slot shows what:
`{"set_slots": {"views": ["structure", "contact"]}}`, or `{"views": ["pae"], "count": 1}` for
one box with tabs.

## Contacts and restraints

```json
{"add_contacts": {"contacts": [[10, 50, 1.0], ["A", 10, "B", 50, 0.5, "#ff0000"]]}}
```

By position index `[i, j, weight, colour?]` or by chain and residue number
`[chainA, resA, chainB, resB, weight, colour?]`. It REPLACES the object's contacts; an empty
list clears them. A contact is a line between two positions - to colour one residue use
`set_color`.

## Side chains and binding sites

```json
"view": {"sidechains": true},
"steps": [
  {"show_sidechains": {"position": {"from": 55, "to": 65}}},
  {"focus": {"chain": "C", "position": 0}}
]
```

`sidechains: true` in `view` is required or there are no atoms to draw. `show_sidechains` /
`hide_sidechains` are relative (add / take away) and run in order. `focus` frames one residue
or ligand with its neighbourhood (side chains of residues within the cutoff) without rotating;
`orient` turns the structure to face the reader and frames a selection; `clip` cuts a slab as
deep as a selection.

## Colour that answers a question

- `set_color` with a literal or a mode, scoped by `name`, `chain` or `position` (not chain and
  position together). Later steps override earlier ones where they overlap.
- `"hydrophobicity"` (Kyte-Doolittle, five bands, grey for non-protein) shows a buried core or
  an exposed patch.
- `"ss"` colours by secondary structure.
- `set_opacity` fades residues so what is behind them shows through - the fix for a side chain
  hidden inside the fold, which no camera angle reveals.

## Several structures

Add several structures; each is an object named for its file (or `name`). They are superposed
on load (`"align": true` default). `{"show_objects": {}}` draws them all at once,
`{"show_objects": {"names": ["apo", "holo"]}}` a subset. Trajectories (multi-model files) share
one timeline; a shorter object HOLDS its last frame by default (`set_frame_policy` with
`"loop"` or `"stretch"` when that is what the data means).

## Check the picture

Render with `render_image` and look at it: an augmentation that is drawn but hidden (behind the
fold, off-frame, the same colour as its neighbour) is the common failure, and only the image
shows it. Re-orient or focus, fade what occludes, and render again.
skills.description: This skill should be used when a py2Dmol view of a structure needs to carry more than the fold - when the user asks to "colour by pLDDT/confidence", "show the PAE", "add a contact map / heatmap", "show contacts / restraints / interactions", "show side chains at the interface", "highlight the binding site", "focus on the ligand", "compare two models / overlay structures", "colour by hydrophobicity", or to make a figure that explains a prediction, a design or a binding mode. Assumes the using-py2Dmol workflow (inspect, spec, validate, render).
skills.name: augmenting-views

skills.body:
# Developing py2Dmol draw plugins

A py2Dmol plugin is a named JavaScript module that returns primitives - lines, dots
(balls) and triangles - in the structure's own model coordinates. The viewer depth-sorts
them with the cartoon in both painters (2D canvas and WebGL2), includes them in PNG and
SVG exports, and carries their payloads through `save_state` / `load_state`. Python only
transports a JSON payload; the plugin defines its meaning.

`py2dmol` is the user's viewer (sokrypton/py2Dmol), never a typo for py3Dmol.

## The two halves

**JavaScript** registers a definition on `window.py2dmolPlugins`, working whether it runs
before or after the library:

```js
(function () {
  var P = window.py2dmolPlugins = window.py2dmolPlugins || {list: [], pending: []};
  var def = {
    name: "mine", version: "1", apiVersion: 1,
    options: {shown: true},          // defaults; a viewer's options merge over them
    key(ctx)    { /* everything that changes prims() - the GPU rebuilds only when it moves */ },
    bounds(ctx) { /* {min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]} in MODEL space, or null - joins fit-to-view */ },
    prims(ctx)  { /* ctx.line(a, b, {color, width}) / ctx.dot(p, {color, radius}) / ctx.tri(a, b, c, {color}) */ },
    // optional: init(host), setPayload(ctx), dispose(ctx)
  };
  if (P.register) P.register(def); else P.pending.push(def);
})();
```

**Python** registers the source once and gives a viewer payloads:

```python
py2Dmol.register_plugin("mine", open("mine.js").read(), version="1")
v = py2Dmol.view()
v.add_pdb("4HHB.cif")
v.add_plugin("mine", {"points": [[0, 0, 0], [10, 0, 0]]}, object=None, frame=None)
v.set_plugin_option("mine", "shown", False)
```

In a view spec (the agent surface) the same thing is
`"plugins": [{"name": "mine", "source": "mine.js", "version": "1"}]` plus a step
`{"add_plugin": {"name": "mine", "payload": {...}}}`.

## Workflow

1. Copy `assets/box.js` as a starting point: it shows `key`, `bounds` and `prims`
   reading `ctx.payloads` and `ctx.options`.
2. Iterate with the plugin check, which runs Python's registration rules and then draws
   the plugin into a real structure in headless Chromium and reports the registry's own
   state:
   ```
   py2dmol plugin-check mine.js mine --payload '{"min":[0,0,0],"max":[10,10,10]}' \
       --structure pdb:1UBQ --out mine.png --json
   ```
   (MCP: the `plugin_check` tool.) `ok: true` needs `registered_in_page`, no `rejected`
   and no `errors`. Look at `mine.png`.
3. Build the real view with a spec and `render_image` to see it in context.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- **Coordinates are model space** - the file's Angstrom, not screen pixels. Use
  `inspect_structure` or the coordinates themselves for scale; `ctx.toView(p)` maps a point
  when needed.
- **`key()` must cover everything `prims()` reads.** The GPU bakes plugin prims into its
  mesh and rebuilds only when the combined key moves; a missing term means a change that
  never appears on the GPU painter while the 2D painter shows it.
- **The budget throws, it does not truncate:** 8,000 primitives per plugin per frame on
  2D (and every SVG export), 60,000 on the GPU. One over drops the whole plugin for that
  frame with an error badge; draw less, or decimate.
- **Non-finite or absurd coordinates drop that primitive** (NaN, Infinity, or more than 50x
  the structure's extent from the view centre). `bounds()` is held to the same rule.
- **Source text may not contain `</script` or `<!--`** - `register_plugin` refuses it. Write
  `"<\/script>"`. Payloads need no escaping; NaN and sets in a payload are refused.
- **Names** match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`.
- **A payload lives on the viewer, not an object**; `object=` / `frame=` only choose where it
  applies. A plugin draws in a viewer only where that viewer has a payload for it.
- **Re-registering the same name** with new code or a new version replaces it (`dispose` is
  called on the old one). Do not rely on `dispose` for per-viewer cleanup.
- **No sandbox.** Plugin JavaScript is inline script in the page, like the core.
- Prims are `noInk` by default (no dark outline); pass `ink: true` to a helper for one.

## Additional resources

- **`references/contract.md`** - the full `ctx` object, helper options, error states,
  framing and the GPU depth-range coupling.
- **`assets/box.js`** - a complete plugin, checked clean with plugin_check.
- In a py2Dmol checkout, `docs/PLUGINS.md` is the authoritative design document and
  `tests/plugin_seam.js`, `tests/plugin_state.py`, `tests/plugin_browser.py` are its tests.
skills.description: This skill should be used when writing, debugging or reviewing a py2Dmol draw plugin - JavaScript that draws extra geometry (lines, balls, triangles) into a py2Dmol viewer alongside the cartoon - or when the user asks to "write a py2Dmol plugin", "draw a box/grid/arrow/mesh/density in py2Dmol", "add custom geometry to the viewer", "register_plugin", "add_plugin", "set_plugin_option", or reports a plugin that draws nothing, is clipped, or shows an error badge.
skills.name: developing-py2Dmol-plugins
resources:
# py2Dmol plugin contract (reference)

Condensed from `docs/PLUGINS.md` in the py2Dmol repository, which is authoritative.

## `ctx`, passed to key / bounds / prims / setPayload / dispose

`renderer`, `host`, `instance` (what `init` returned), `name`, `version`, `apiVersion`,
`options`, `payloads` (`[{object, frame, payload, index}]` - only those that apply to what
is drawn now), `frame`, `maxPrims`, `painter` (`'2d'`, `'gpu'` or `'svg'`), `scale`,
`toView(p, objectName?)`, `project(x, y, z)`, and the three helpers below.

`init(host)` runs once per viewer; `host = {renderer, viewerId, requestRender()}`.

## Helpers

| helper | options | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.line(a, b, {color, width, ink})` | `width` Angstrom, default 0.35 | joints are added for you |
| `ctx.dot(p, {color, radius, ink})` | `radius` Angstrom, default 0.5 | colour baked; recolouring the structure leaves it alone |
| `ctx.tri(a, b, c, {color})` | | opaque, flat-shaded, double-sided, lit by its own normal |

Colour: `[r,g,b]`, `{r,g,b}` or `'#rrggbb'`. Each helper returns `false` and drops the
primitive for a point behind the camera (perspective), a non-finite coordinate, or one more
than 50x the structure's extent (never less than 500 A) from the view centre; the plugin then
shows an error state counting the drops.

## Budget

Defaults 2D 8,000 and GPU 60,000 primitives per plugin per frame
(`window.py2dmolPlugins.caps`, changeable by a host page before a viewer renders). Over the
cap the helper throws `PluginBudgetError`; the plugin draws nothing that frame and says so on
the console, in a badge inside the viewer, and in `py2dmolPlugins.errors(renderer)`. An SVG
export is always the 2D painter and so the 2D cap; it writes the refusal as an XML comment in
the file. Any other exception in `prims` is treated the same way and its partial output is
rolled back.

## Error states

`py2dmolPlugins.rejected` - refusals at registration (`{name, message}`).
`py2dmolPlugins.errors(renderer)` - `[{name, message, painter}]`, painter one of
`'2d'`, `'gpu'`, `'svg'`, or `'load'` for `init` / `setPayload` / `key` / `bounds`.
`register()` returns the definition, the existing one (same name and version), or `null` for
a refusal; it never throws.

## Framing

`bounds(ctx)` becomes a radius about the view centre and floors the FITTED span (per axis),
so the default view and every "orient to everything" frame the plugin. A span set by orient
to a selection, focus, or the app is not floored, so focusing one residue can still zoom
inside a shell drawn around it. A plugin that arrives after the opening orient is framed at
the next orient to everything.

## GPU depth range

Plugin strokes are folded into the GPU's depth range so a shape larger than the structure is
not clipped. The cost: a plugin reaching well past the structure (measured at 2.9x its radius
on 1CRN) moves about 1% of the cartoon's ink on the GPU through depth tie-breaks; inside the
radius it costs nothing.

## State

`save_state` writes payloads under a top-level `plugins` key (only when there are any), and
the website's session file does the same. An unknown plugin in a loaded state is kept
verbatim with one warning.

## Tube style

Both styles draw plugins. The GPU tube draws lines and balls as capsules and hands any frame
with a plugin triangle to the 2D tube.

skills.body:
# Embedding py2Dmol in a web page py2Dmol's embed API is one script tag and one call. No Python and no build step: ```html
``` `py2Dmol.show(target, text, options)` creates the canvas inside `target` (an element or its id), detects mmCIF vs PDB from the text, and returns the viewer. `py2Dmol.fetch(id)` returns a structure's text: four characters go to the PDB, anything else to AlphaFold DB. `assets/minimal.html` is a complete page to copy. ## Choose the bundle first | file | painter | pick it when | |---|---|---| | `py2Dmol.embed.min.js` | WebGL2 | the default; large structures stay smooth | | `py2Dmol.embed.cpu.min.js` | 2D canvas | no WebGL2, or SVG export is needed | | `py2Dmol.full.min.js` | both, plus the whole web app | the page wants the app's sequence strip, MSA, sessions, file ingestion or TM-align | - **Neither embed bundle falls back to the other.** The WebGL2 build on a browser without WebGL2 draws nothing and says so on the console. There is no `gpu` option - passing one throws; the file decides the painter. - **`full` needs two script tags:** `align/align.js` is loaded separately (as `index.html` does) because no bundle contains it; every alignment method throws until it is loaded. ## Options to `show` `width`, `height` (default: the element's size), `style` (`tube` default, `richardson`, `ribbon`, `3d`), `color` (`auto`, `chain`, `rainbow`, `plddt`, `deepmind`, `ss`, `hydrophobicity`), `bg` (`3d` defaults to black), `box`, `name`, `biounit` (default true - build the biological assembly), `orient` (default true), `select` (click picks a residue), `controls` (the Style panel), `play` (frame strip; on by itself for multi-model files). Anything else is viewer configuration: `detail` (2-8), `shadow`, `outline`, `ortho`, `colorblind`, `rotate`, `autoplay`, `cyclic`, `heatmap: {enabled: true}`. ## The selector (one grammar for every verb) `'B'` a chain; `[3, 4, 5]` positions; or an object whose keys narrow each other: `{chain}`, `{positions}`, `{range: [a, b]}` (half open), `{residues}` (the file's numbering), `{type: 'L'|'P'|'N'}`, `{near: sel}` (within 5 A, atom to atom), `{angstroms}`, `{object}`, `{not: sel}`. `{chain: 'B', residues: [12]}` is one residue. An unknown key throws. **Positions are not residue numbers.** A position counts from zero across everything drawn (one per residue, one per ligand atom); a residue number is the file's. Both are integers and nothing warns when one is passed for the other. Prefer `{chain, residues}` when the file's numbering is what is known. ## Common verbs `v.setStyle(name)`, `v.setColor(colour, sel?)` (colours accumulate until a mode is set again), `v.orient(sel?)`, `v.clip(sel)` / `v.clip()`, `v.select(sel)` / `v.unselect(sel)`, `v.hide(sel)` / `v.show(sel)` / `v.resetVisibility()`, `v.showSidechains(sel)` / `v.hideSidechains(sel)`, `v.setSidechainColor(colour, sel?)`, `v.setContacts(list, name?)`, `v.load(text, name)`, `v.showObjects(names)`, `v.setFrame(i)`, `v.toImage({format, dpi})`. Full table and the animation and alignment calls: `references/api.md`. ## Traps - **Panels need the host's markup.** A panel finds its own elements and does nothing until they exist: the heatmap wants `#heatmapContainer` holding `#heatmapCanvas` (the older `#paeContainer` / `#paeCanvas` still work). Put panel markup BESIDE the viewer's element, never inside - `show()` replaces its container's children. And `controls: true` is what mounts panels at all on the embed path. - **Two viewers on one page:** the PAE/heatmap panel scopes to its container; the full app's sequence strip and MSA look elements up on `document`, so two of those would find each other's. - **Animate with `replaceFrame`, not `addFrame`.** Morphing between conformations by appending frames fills the play bar with steps that are not frames of anything. Parse once with `py2Dmol.framesFromText`, then `v.replaceFrame(frame)` per step: the frame count never moves and the camera stays put. - **Elements need element columns.** Element colouring of ligands and side chains reads PDB columns 77-78; garbage there (e.g. a serial number) colours every atom one flat colour. - **A host stylesheet can reach the viewer's controls.** The shell scopes its own CSS, but a page rule on bare `button` still applies margins; style the page's own buttons by class. ## Additional resources - **`references/api.md`** - the complete verb table, frames and animation, `superpose`, contacts across structures, and the full-app doors (`py2dmolLoadFiles`). - **`assets/minimal.html`** - a working page. - `https://py2dmol.solab.org/embed.html` - every call above, running; in a checkout, `embed.html` is the specification `tests/embed.py` checks.
skills.description: This skill should be used when putting a py2Dmol viewer on a web page with no Python - when the user asks to "embed a structure in a web page", "add a protein viewer to my site/app", "use py2Dmol from JavaScript", "py2Dmol.show", "which py2Dmol bundle", "show a PAE/heatmap on my page", "animate a structure in the browser", or is wiring py2Dmol into a host app (LocalFold-style) with its own markup. Covers bundle choice, the show() options, the selector grammar, the panels' markup requirements and the traps that make an embed draw nothing.
skills.name: embedding-py2Dmol

# py2Dmol embed API (reference) Condensed from `embed.html`, which is the specification (`tests/embed.py` reads its code samples and checks every call against a running viewer). ## Module functions | call | does | |---|---| | `py2Dmol.show(target, text, options)` | build a viewer in `target` from PDB/mmCIF text; returns it | | `py2Dmol.fetch(id)` | promise of a structure's text: 4 chars -> RCSB, else AlphaFold DB. Rejects on a bad id | | `py2Dmol.frameFromText(text)` | one frame object from a file's text | | `py2Dmol.framesFromText(text)` | every model in a file as frames | | `py2Dmol.superpose(mobile, reference, {from, to})` | Kabsch fit computed on the index arrays `from`/`to` (e.g. alpha carbons), applied to every point of `mobile`. Works when the two differ in length (a mutant on its parent). A bad index throws | | `py2Dmol.hydrophobicityBands` | the five Kyte-Doolittle bands, for a legend | ## Looking | call | does | |---|---| | `v.setStyle(name)` | `tube`, `richardson`, `ribbon`, `3d` | | `v.setColor(colour, sel?)` | a mode for everything, or a colour on part of it; colours accumulate until a mode is set again | | `v.orient(sel?)` | frame that, the selection, or everything visible; `{animate: false}` jumps | | `v.clip(sel)` | a slab as deep as the selection, refitted as it turns; `v.clip()` turns it off | | `v.render(reason)` | redraw (the verbs above already do) | | `v.toImage({format, dpi, transparent, dataUrl})` | promise of `{blob, format, width, height, dpi, text, dataUrl?}`; `svg` needs the 2D painter (the cpu bundle) | ## Selecting and visibility | call | does | |---|---| | `v.select(sel)` / `v.unselect(sel)` | add to / take from the selection; `unselect()` clears | | `v.hide(sel)` / `v.show(sel)` | subtract from / add to what is drawn | | `v.resetVisibility()` | draw everything; `resetVisibility()` then `hide({not: sel})` shows only `sel` | | `v.showSidechains(sel)` / `v.hideSidechains(sel)` | draw / remove side-chain atoms (relative) | | `v.setSidechainColor(colour, sel?)` | a colour or a mode for the side chains alone; `null` follows the residue again. Only the carbon skeleton changes - O stays red, N blue | | `v.showElements(sel)` / `v.hideElements(sel)` | element colouring of atoms (on by default for ligands and drawn side chains) | | `v.setVisibility(patch)` / `v.getVisibility()` | the lower level under hide/show; prefer those | ## Structures and frames | call | does | |---|---| | `v.load(text, name)` | another structure under its own name; loading over a name replaces it | | `v.showObjects(names)` | which structures are drawn together | | `v.setFrame(i)` | step to a frame | | `v.addFrame(frame, name)` | append a frame (a trajectory) | | `v.replaceFrame(frame, name?)` | replace the LAST frame - for animation; the count never moves | | `v.addObject(name)` | an empty object to add frames to | | `v.resetAll()` | back to an empty viewer | | `v.setSlots(['pae', 'structure'])` | what each slot shows (structure, a map key, scatter) | ## Contacts `v.setContacts(list, name?)` replaces; an empty list clears. Within one object an end is a position or a chain-and-residue pair: ```js v.setContacts([[5, 60, 1.0], [10, 40, 0.4, {r: 255, g: 0, b: 0}]]); v.setContacts([['A', 12, 'B', 34, 1.0]]); ``` An end written as a one-residue selector may be in a different structure; such a contact belongs to the viewer, so pass no name: ```js v.setContacts([[{object: 'ubiquitin', residues: [10]}, {object: 'copy', residues: [40]}, 1.0]]); ``` ## A heatmap beside the structure ```html
``` `embed.html` section 16 computes a contact map from the drawn alpha carbons and attaches it with `replaceFrame`. ## The full app's doors (`py2Dmol.full.min.js`) - `py2dmolLoadFiles(files, loadAsFrames, groupName)` - ingestion with virtual files `{name, readAsync}`; the extension decides the kind (`.pdb`/`.cif` structure, `.json` PAE paired by basename, `.a3m`/`.fasta` alignment, `.cst` contacts). - `py2dmolReadyMessage` - replaces the idle status line. - Host the parts of `index.html`'s markup whose features are wanted; each panel needs its own elements.

skills.body:
# Using py2Dmol

py2Dmol (sokrypton/py2Dmol) is a protein structure viewer: a Python package for notebooks
and a web app. **It is never a typo for py3Dmol** - do not substitute py3Dmol, nglview or
matplotlib for it.

## Two ways in

| context | use |
|---|---|
| A notebook (Jupyter, Colab) a person is reading | the Python API: `v = py2Dmol.view(...)`, `v.add_pdb(...)`, `v.show()` |
| An agent, a script, a pipeline - anything with no notebook | the **view spec** through the `py2dmol` CLI or the `py2dmol` MCP tools |

`show()` outside a notebook prints `<IPython.core.display.HTML object>` and nothing else -
never use it from a script or agent. Use a spec and `render_html` / `render_image`, or
`v.save_html(path)` from Python.

## The agent workflow

1. **Inspect** - `inspect_structure` (`py2dmol inspect <path | pdb:1UBQ | afdb:Q5VSL9> --json`).
   It reports every chain's and ligand's range of drawn positions, residue numbers,
   sequences and whether the B-factor column looks like a pLDDT. Write selectors from this,
   not from memory of the PDB entry.
2. **Write a spec** - one JSON document; call `vocabulary` (`py2dmol vocab --json`) for every
   legal key, read off the installed code.
3. **Validate** - `validate_spec`. Every problem comes back at once, each with a JSON path and
   the allowed values; fix and repeat until `valid: true`.
4. **Render** - `render_html` for an interactive page (opens from `file://`), `render_image`
   for a PNG/SVG to look at. Look at the image before calling the work done.
5. Optionally `save_state` - a state file a person can open in a notebook
   (`view.load_state`) or on the website.

A minimal spec:

```json
{
  "spec": 1,
  "view": {"style": "cartoon", "color": "plddt", "size": [600, 600]},
  "structures": [{"source": "afdb:Q5VSL9"}],
  "steps": [{"orient": {}}]
}
```

`steps` run in order; each is `{verb: {arguments}}` with the verb a `view` method
(`set_color`, `show_sidechains`, `add_contacts`, `orient`, `focus`, `clip`, `set_slots`,
`add_plugin`, ...). Arguments are that method's own keywords.

## Selectors: the three rules that catch everyone

1. **`position` indexes what the object DRAWS**, not residue numbers and not an index within
   a chain: one position per polymer residue and one per **ligand atom**, across all chains,
   from 0. Ligand atoms sit between chains - on 4HHB chain A is positions 0-141, its heme
   141-184, chain B starts at 184. Take ranges from `inspect_structure`.
2. **A range is `{"from": a, "to": b}` (b excluded).** A JSON list `[40, 60]` means exactly
   positions 40 and 60. (In Python, `position=(40, 60)` is the range; JSON has no tuple.)
3. **`set_color` refuses `chain` and `position` together** - write two steps.

## Defaults worth knowing

- **Styles:** `tube` (default), `cartoon` (= `richardson`), `ribbon`, `3d`. `3d` puts the
  picture on black unless `bg` says otherwise.
- **Colour modes:** `auto`, `chain`, `plddt`, `deepmind`, `rainbow`, `ss`, `hydrophobicity`,
  `entropy` (needs an MSA). A literal colour (`"#ff8800"`, `"red"`) works anywhere a mode does.
- **The biological assembly is built by default** (`use_biounit: true`). When it expands the
  structure, gemmi renames chains (`A` -> `A1`, `A2`, ...). `inspect_structure` reports the
  names actually drawn; pass `"use_biounit": false` for the deposited asymmetric unit.
- **Side chains need `"sidechains": true` in `view`** before `show_sidechains` can draw any.
- Fetched ids are cached in the directory `vocabulary` reports under `cache_dir`
  (`PY2DMOL_CACHE_DIR`, `[tool.py2dmol] cache_dir`, or `~/.config/py2dmol/config.toml`);
  with none configured they go to a per-process temp dir, never the working directory.

## CLI exit codes

0 ok, 2 agent extra missing, 3 invalid spec/argument, 4 file or id not found, 5 screenshot
extra or browser missing, 6 the page drew nothing in time, 7 malformed config. Add `--json`
for machine-readable output.

## Installing

`pip install "py2Dmol[agent]"` (Python >= 3.13) for the CLI and MCP server;
`pip install "py2Dmol[screenshot]"` then `py2dmol screenshot-setup` for `render_image`. The
plain `pip install py2Dmol` notebook package needs neither.

## Related skills

- **augmenting-views** - adding meaning to a structure: confidence, heatmaps, contacts, side
  chains, focus, several objects.
- **developing-py2Dmol-plugins** - drawing custom geometry into the viewer.
skills.description: This skill should be used whenever a protein, nucleic-acid or ligand structure needs to be shown, rendered, or turned into a figure or interactive page with py2Dmol - including when the user asks to "show this structure", "render a PDB/CIF", "make a picture of the fold", "visualize an AlphaFold model", "look at the binding site", "use py2dmol", or mentions py2Dmol, the py2dmol CLI or the py2dmol MCP tools. Also covers driving py2Dmol from a notebook versus from an agent, and the selector rules that make most first attempts colour the wrong residues.
